title and abstract.summary: The study evaluated changes in species diversity and six functional traits (trophic level, seasonal duration, body size, elevational range, nesting position, and soil dependency) for different feeding guilds within the Aculeata community along an elevational gradient in a boreal forest in northern Japan.

introduction.summary: The study aimed to clarify whether the pattern of species diversity (SD) and trait response differs between feeding guilds in an Aculeata community along an elevational gradient in a boreal forest in eastern Hokkaido, northern Japan.

methods.summary: The study measured the collection of Aculeata bees and wasps using yellow pan traps across different elevation sites in the Ashoro Research Forest and Mt. Kumaneshiri-dake.

results.summary: This study measured various ecological metrics, such as species richness (SR), species diversity (SD), and distribution indices (FD, CWM), across different feeding guilds (pollinators, predators, parasitoids) and the entire Aculeata community in relation to increasing elevation. The measurements covered multiple species within the Aculeata group, with Lasioglossum problematicum being specifically noted for its abundance and elevation range.
